findings.claim: Every decision-table row and every `_demo` assertion passes `token=` explicitly, so `gate.py`'s `token is None` branch — the only one `app.py` takes — is exercised by nothing. A three-line `return True` there bills every anonymous request on an UNCONFIGURED deployment with the gate green.
findings.acceptance: At least one row calling `paid_path_open(presented, armed)` with NO `token=` keyword, asserting False when the secret is unset and the same verdict as the explicit-token row when configured, watched red on that edit.
findings.resolution: FIVE such rows in `check_escalation_door`, called exactly as `_run` calls the door — two positional arguments, the secret moved in the environment with `_patched_env` instead: (unset, header set) -> closed; (unset, no header) -> closed; (empty, header set) -> closed; (configured, no header) -> closed; (configured, header set) -> OPEN. Each also compares its verdict against the explicit-`token=` call for the same secret, so the nine rows above it cannot certify a branch they never enter. Four matching assertions added to `gate.py::_demo`, which had the same gap, so the module self-check the CI unit job runs also covers the production branch.
findings.verified: M3 — `if token is None: return True, …` above the token normalisation — invariant exit 1 (84/85). Table in pr61-r2-red.txt PART 1c, mutation in PART 2.

findings.claim: The check pins that `paid_path_open` is called once in `_run` and that its verdict flows onward; it never inspects the call's ARGUMENTS. `request.headers.get(gate.HEADER, gate.configured_token())` lets an anonymous request in and makes the envelope claim a valid header was presented; a literal `True` as the second argument defeats the operator's runaway stop while `/api/meta` still publishes `escalation_enabled: false`.
findings.acceptance: Assert both operands — a read of `gate.HEADER` off the request parameter, and the module's off-switch constant — watched red on both.
findings.resolution: The door's one call site now has both operands asserted. First argument: exactly one `<request>.headers.get(...)`, the object must be the `request` PARAMETER, the call must take exactly ONE argument (a default is the exploit, and it is named as such in the failure message), and that argument must be `gate.HEADER` rather than a retyped string. Second argument: `ast.Name` equal to the module's off-switch constant, configurable via `input.off_switch`.
findings.verified: M4 (the secret as the header's default) invariant exit 1 (84/85); M6 (`True` for the off-switch) invariant exit 1 (84/85). Both in pr61-r2-red.txt PART 2.

findings.claim: `extract.py:160` still says the trigger stays quiet on '42 of 43 dev fixtures, every real EDGAR filing in the set'; the second half is false, and the same commit corrected `extract.py:8` and `escalate.py` while missing this line eight below.
findings.acceptance: extract.py:160 reads 42 of 44 and drops or corrects the claim; ideally the census sites are bound the way `_index_h2_money` binds INDEX.md to §h2.
findings.resolution: Both. The line reads '42 of 44 dev fixtures, and 28 of the 29 real EDGAR filings among them', names `intc-2025` as the exception, and records that it went stale eight lines below a header the same commit corrected. The census is now BOUND, in the sweep that already derives the true corpus: `check_deployed_exclusion_derived` asserts every `<n> of <m> dev|real` across five files carries the denominator it measured (44 dev, 29 real), with the dev/real split read from `d11_trigger_scan.py`'s own SYNTHETIC roster rather than a second copy. DENOMINATORS only, and the reason is in the code: the numerators are different statistics per site (fires, stays quiet, refuses before any item) and pinning each would mean re-deriving each — the corpus size is the part that goes stale for everyone at once, which is what happened. `src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py` is deliberately outside the pinned set (its '18 of 43 dev documents' is rung 1's window-offset statistic, PR #58 R17, which this sweep does not re-derive); pinning a denominator whose numerator nothing checks would be the vacuity this PR is about.
findings.verified: N11 (the exact R21 line reverted) fast exit 1; N12 (README's real-filing rate) exit 1; N13 (escalate.py's quiet count) exit 1. The pin's FIRST revision left N11 green — it matched a literal space where the wrapped sentence has a newline — which the artifact records, because it was caught by running the mutation and not by reading the regex.
findings.cost: No new case and no new sweep: the assertions ride the `deployed-exclusion-derived` run that already extracts all 44 fixtures. `fast` measured 4.46s for that check, unchanged.
